fields.title: Identifying Misinformation in a Viral World
fields.content:
The Challenge of Viral Rumors

In Kenya, false or misleading information spreads incredibly fast across platforms like WhatsApp, TikTok, and X (formerly Twitter). Misinformation often dresses up as legitimate breaking news to trick unsuspecting citizens.

  • Emotional Triggers: Fake news often tries to make you feel angry, shocked, or fearful.
  • The Forwarding Problem: Forwarded messages on WhatsApp frequently strip away the original source, leaving no accountability.

fields.title: Misinformation, Disinformation & Malinformation
fields.content:
Defining the Spectrum of Falsehoods

Not all false information shared online shares the same motive. Academics and journalists divide it into three distinct categories based on intent:

  • Misinformation: False info shared without any bad intentions (e.g., a relative sharing an unverified health tip thinking it helps).
  • Disinformation: Information that is deliberately created or shared to deceive, harm, or manipulate people.
  • Malinformation: Real, genuine information shared out of context or leaked maliciously to cause harm.

fields.title: Elections, Propaganda, and Disinformation
fields.content:
The Machinery of Political Trolls

During democratic processes, coordinated online networks often deploy intentional disinformation campaigns. These groups use paid influencers, automated bots, and heavily biased narratives to sway public opinion or create artificial divisions.

  • Coordinated Behavior: Multiple distinct accounts posting identical text strings simultaneously.
  • Astroturfing: Creating the fake appearance of a grassroots movement when it's actually funded by a centralized political operator.

fields.title: Manipulated Media: Fabricating Kenyan News
fields.content:
The Threat of Cloned Graphics

A highly prevalent tactic in Kenya involves digital manipulation of mainstream newspaper front pages. Scammers use photo editing software to change the lead headlines on digital images of papers like The Daily Nation or The Standard before sharing them online.

  • Visual Inspection: Look closely for font mismatches, odd alignment, or low-resolution text patches.
  • Cross-Verification: Always visit the media house's official social channels or e-paper platform to check the real headline for that day.

fields.title: Inside PesaCheck's Verification System
fields.content:
How the Experts Debunk Rumors

Professional fact-checking desks don't guess; they follow rigorous investigative pathways to verify claims floating around East Africa.

  • Primary Source Sourcing: Contacting government ministries, corporate spokespeople, or scientists directly to verify claims rather than relying on hearsay.
  • Database Checks: Checking national registries, official gazettes, and official economic data databases to evaluate financial claims.

fields.title: The Pillars of Local Fact-Checking
fields.content:
Key Steps to Take Yourself

You don't need a journalism degree to start fact-checking everyday messages. Veteran editors rely on simple, repetitive investigative routines:

  • Lateral Reading: Opening new browser tabs to find out what independent sources say about a website instead of just relying on the site's own 'About' description.
  • Contextual Tracking: Checking when an image or quote was originally generated to ensure it isn't old media passed off as happening today.

fields.title: Digital Forensics & Verification Desks
fields.content:
Putting Forensic Tools to Work

When claims use manipulated visual assets, simple observation might fail. This is where dedicated digital investigative forensics tools come in.

  • Reverse Image Search: Tools like Google Lens, TinEye, and Yandex help uncover where an image originally appeared.
  • Domain Spoofing Check: Scammers clone trusted names using weird extensions (e.g., using citizen.news-kenya.co instead of the real domain). Always verify domain architecture.

fields.title: Unmasking AI and Deepfakes in Kenya
fields.content:
Spotting Synthetic Audio and Video

Generative AI now allows bad actors to create highly realistic voice clones of political leaders or fabricated videos of public figures saying things they never did.

  • Audio Indicators: Listen closely for flat emotional delivery, unexpected metallic robotic echoes, or unnatural breathing pauses.
  • Visual Artifacts: Check for strange blurring patterns around the lips, missing teeth definitions, or reflections inside eyes that don't match ambient lighting.

fields.title: Final Exam Instructions
fields.content:
Welcome to your Capstone Assessment

You have successfully journeyed through fake news identification, content classifications, lateral reading, and forensic tool execution. Now it is time to prove your skills.

  • This comprehensive exam features critical thinking questions.
  • The focus is entirely on realistic media environment challenges faced in daily life.
  • A passing score secures your 'Truth Defender' course completion badge. Good luck!

fields.text: When a person shares an unverified forward on WhatsApp thinking they are helping their family, what are they spreading?
fields.choice_a: Disinformation
fields.choice_b: Misinformation
fields.choice_c: Malinformation
fields.choice_d: Satire

fields.text: What defines 'Disinformation' compared to other forms of fake news?
fields.choice_a: It is always published in physical newspapers.
fields.choice_b: It is false information shared with a deliberate intent to deceive or cause harm.
fields.choice_c: It is completely true but boring.
fields.choice_d: It can only be spread by verified social media accounts.

fields.text: Why do false claims spread so rapidly in Kenyan WhatsApp groups?
fields.choice_a: Because WhatsApp automatically verifies all links.
fields.choice_b: Because forwarded messages often lack context, hiding the original source.
fields.choice_c: Because all WhatsApp groups are public.
fields.choice_d: Because users must pay to read real news.

fields.text: Which of these describes 'Malinformation'?
fields.choice_a: Completely made-up scientific data.
fields.choice_b: A parody article from a comedy website.
fields.choice_c: Genuine, real information shared out of context specifically to cause harm.
fields.choice_d: An honest typo made by a mainstream journalist.

fields.text: What is the most common reason fake news creators use highly emotional headlines?
fields.choice_a: To bypass the reader's critical thinking and spark immediate clicks or shares.
fields.choice_b: To adhere to strict journalistic ethics codes.
fields.choice_c: To ensure their grammar is correct.
fields.choice_d: To cut down the length of the article text.

fields.text: What is 'astroturfing' in online political campaigns?
fields.choice_a: Planting real grass around government buildings.
fields.choice_b: Artificially creating the false impression of widespread organic public support.
fields.choice_c: Using satellite imagery to verify news claims.
fields.choice_d: Deleting old posts from political candidates.

fields.text: You see an image of a prominent Kenyan newspaper front page with a shocking headline. How should you verify it?
fields.choice_a: Assume it is real and forward it to your groups immediately.
fields.choice_b: Check the media house's official, verified social media channels or official e-paper site to see if the headlines match.
fields.choice_c: Ask a friend if they think it looks real.
fields.choice_d: Look at the colors in the background.

fields.text: Which of these is a common visual warning sign of a manipulated news graphic?
fields.choice_a: The article uses standard black font color.
fields.choice_b: Mismatched font styles, strange alignment, or blurry text boxes over a clear image.
fields.choice_c: The presence of a correct date stamp.
fields.choice_d: A high-resolution photograph of the journalist.

fields.text: What is the primary role of an 'online influencer farm' during election cycles?
fields.choice_a: To teach local farmers how to market their produce online.
fields.choice_b: To systematically push paid political narratives and amplify attacks against opponents.
fields.choice_c: To fact-check political statements impartially.
fields.choice_d: To provide technical support for election voting equipment.

fields.text: Why do digital news falsifiers target trusted mainstream brands like The Daily Nation or The Standard?
fields.choice_a: To help those brands get more print subscribers.
fields.choice_b: To hijack the brand's hard-earned public credibility to make a lie believable.
fields.choice_c: Because those brands don't have websites.
fields.choice_d: To test out new image editing software features.

fields.text: When a professional fact-checker encounters a viral claim about a new law, what is their first step?
fields.choice_a: They write an opinion piece about why the law is bad.
fields.choice_b: They locate the primary source, such as the official Kenya Gazette or parliament records.
fields.choice_c: They count how many likes the post has.
fields.choice_d: They delete the post from social media accounts.

fields.text: What is 'Lateral Reading'?
fields.choice_a: Reading text sideways to spot secret codes.
fields.choice_b: Leaving a web page to open multiple tabs and cross-verify the credentials and claims of that source against other reputable inputs.
fields.choice_c: Skimming only the right side of a paragraph.
fields.choice_d: Translating an article into multiple local languages.

fields.text: Which of these is considered a 'primary source' for verification?
fields.choice_a: An unverified video analysis by an anonymous TikToker.
fields.choice_b: An official, stamped public statement released on an official government portal.
fields.choice_c: A blog post summarizing what a newspaper said.
fields.choice_d: A trending hashtag on social media.

fields.text: Why do fact-checkers verify when an image was first uploaded to the internet?
fields.choice_a: To see if the image files are too large for mobile phones.
fields.choice_b: To ensure an old event or photo is not being falsely repurposed as evidence of a current incident.
fields.choice_c: To find out what type of camera the photographer used.
fields.choice_d: To copyright check the photograph for profit.

fields.text: What organization is a prominent independent fact-checking platform active across Kenya and East Africa?
fields.choice_a: The Onion News Desk
fields.choice_b: PesaCheck
fields.choice_c: Reddit Kenya
fields.choice_d: Wikipedia Admin Group

fields.text: Which specific tool is best suited to trace the true original online appearance of an uploaded image file?
fields.choice_a: Google Docs
fields.choice_b: TinEye or Google Lens Reverse Search
fields.choice_c: Adobe Photoshop Editor
fields.choice_d: Microsoft Excel

fields.text: You encounter a news blog operating under the URL 'ntv-kenya.com.co'. What should this suffix make you suspect?
fields.choice_a: It is an official high-speed premium server link.
fields.choice_b: It is a domain-spoofing attempt attempting to masquerade as NTV Kenya.
fields.choice_c: It is the exclusive site for mobile phone browsers.
fields.choice_d: It means the site is protected by government security encryption.

fields.text: What is a common sign that an online video of a public figure might be an AI deepfake?
fields.choice_a: The video length is longer than two minutes.
fields.choice_b: Unnatural lip movements, strange eye-blinking patterns, and shifting skin textures near the jawline.
fields.choice_c: The speaker is wearing an official suit jacket.
fields.choice_d: The recording was taken outdoors during daylight.

fields.text: When assessing suspected AI voice clones of famous individuals, what should you listen for?
fields.choice_a: Background traffic noises.
fields.choice_b: Unnatural cadence, lack of realistic breathing patterns, and flat robotic phrasing tones.
fields.choice_c: A loud volume setting.
fields.choice_d: The use of local Swahili phrases.

fields.text: What is the official domain structure used exclusively by authentic Kenyan Government ministries and departments?
fields.choice_a: go.ke
fields.choice_b: com.ke
fields.choice_c: org.ke
fields.choice_d: gov.com

fields.text: If someone accidentally forwards a fake medical cure on social media without knowing it is false, this is called:
fields.choice_a: Disinformation
fields.choice_b: Misinformation
fields.choice_c: Malinformation
fields.choice_d: Satire

fields.text: Which of these domain architectures should you trust most for an official announcement about national tax policies?
fields.choice_a: kra-portal-updates.com
fields.choice_b: kra.go.ke
fields.choice_c: kra-news.co.ke
fields.choice_d: kenya-revenue-authority.org.co

fields.text: Coordinated networks using paid actors or bot clusters to push a custom trending hashtag during an election is an example of:
fields.choice_a: Lateral Reading
fields.choice_b: Astroturfing Disinformation
fields.choice_c: Objective Media Reporting
fields.choice_d: Reverse Image Searching

fields.text: What does a successful 'Reverse Image Search' help a media user discover?
fields.choice_a: The identity of everyone who liked the photo.
fields.choice_b: The historical origins, early upload dates, and true contexts of an image asset.
fields.choice_c: How to edit out objects from the photograph.
fields.choice_d: The camera model serial number.

fields.text: Why is relying solely on a website's 'About Us' section a poor confirmation practice?
fields.choice_a: Because 'About Us' sections are always too long to read completely.
fields.choice_b: Because bad actors can easily fabricate an impressive, professional-sounding description about themselves.
fields.choice_c: Because search engines don't index 'About Us' pages.
fields.choice_d: Because news sites do not have these pages.

fields.text: A trending audio file appears online showing a regional politician saying something shocking, but it sounds metallic and lacks common breathing pauses. What should you evaluate for?
fields.choice_a: A bad micro-SD card connection.
fields.choice_b: An AI generative voice clone attempt.
fields.choice_c: Standard local broadcast interference.
fields.choice_d: The speed settings on your media player.

fields.text: When cross-checking a viral claim, what is the value of independent platforms like PesaCheck or Africa Check?
fields.choice_a: They provide fast, entertaining commentary on internet trends.
fields.choice_b: They apply transparent, non-partisan verification workflows to back up or debunk local claims.
fields.choice_c: They block false websites from opening on Kenyan phones.
fields.choice_d: They provide free mobile data bundles to users.

fields.text: What psychological trap causes people to immediately trust a fake news story simply because it matches their existing political views?
fields.choice_a: The Reverse Search Effect
fields.choice_b: Confirmation Bias
fields.choice_c: Astroturfing Illusion
fields.choice_d: Domain Ambiguity

fields.text: What is the best immediate reaction when a family member sends a shocking 'breaking news' link with the tag 'Forwarded Many Times' into your group?
fields.choice_a: Forward it to your other networks immediately to be safe.
fields.choice_b: Pause, read laterally, and check trusted local media outlets or fact-checkers before taking action.
fields.choice_c: Ignore the message completely and leave the group chat.
fields.choice_d: Reply immediately with an angry emoji.

fields.title: Spotting WhatsApp Broadcast Scams
fields.article_headline: Nairobi County Government Announces Free Fuel to Every Citizen Tomorrow!
fields.article_meta: Forwarded Many Times | WhatsApp Broadcast Alert
fields.article_body: BREAKING NEWS: To ease economic pressure, the Nairobi County Government has just announced that all local petrol stations will give out free fuel to citizens tomorrow only! YOU MUST CLICK THIS UNKNOWN LINK IMMEDIATELY TO REGISTER BEFORE MIDNIGHT: http://nairobi-free-fuel.scam-link.net !!! Share this widely!

fields.title: Dissecting Cloned Graphics
fields.article_headline: CLONED HEADLINE: Parliament Votes to Increase Taxes on WhatsApp to 80%!
fields.article_meta: Graphic shared widely on X (formerly Twitter) | 5,000 Reposts
fields.article_body: A highly viral digital image designed to look like a prominent Kenyan newspaper's front page has circulated on social media. The lead headline reads 'WHATSAPP TAX TRIPLE' and claims Parliament has passed an immediate law to tax the messaging app. However, close observation reveals the headline uses different fonts, displays uneven letter alignments, and shows pixelated blurring directly around the borders of the text. A check of the official e-paper shows the real headline for today was completely different.

fields.title: Investigating Viral Environmental Rumors
fields.article_headline: Viral Post: Lion Spotted Roaming Free Along Mombasa Road Traffic Today!
fields.article_meta: Shared by AlertKenya On Facebook | 12,000 shares
fields.article_body: A viral Facebook post warns: 'Terrifying news! A huge male lion has escaped Nairobi National Park and is currently walking right down Mombasa Road next to the Express Way. Avoid the area completely!' The post includes a photo of a lion next to a highway barrier. However, no local drivers have confirmed this, KWS social media pages are completely silent, and a reverse image search reveals the photo was taken in a South African game reserve in 2017.

fields.title: Evaluating Spoofed Domains
fields.article_headline: Urgent: Ministry of Education Announces Closure of All Schools Starting Friday!
fields.article_body: Urgent announcement! Due to unexpected policy adjustments, the Ministry of Education has directed all primary and secondary schools to send students home indefinitely starting this Friday. Parents must click the link below to download the mandatory transport refund form on this non-governmental portal.

fields.label: No official named spokesperson or verified mainstream media source is cited
Uses urgent, alarming language and multiple exclamation marks to create artificial pressure
The text contains standard, professional formatting guidelines
Urges the reader to click a highly suspicious, non-governmental link to register
The main headline font style differs noticeably from the standard typography of the newspaper
The official logo of the media company is displayed in the upper corner
The official daily e-paper archives show a completely different lead story for that exact date
There is visible digital artifacting and blurry pixel boxes around the letters of the headline
A reverse search reveals the associated photo was taken in a different country years ago
The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) official verified social accounts have released no alerts
The text lists Mombasa Road as the location of the incident
No secondary reports, eyewitness videos, or mainstream traffic reporters have confirmed the sighting
The URL is a spoofed domain instead of the official 'education.go.ke' domain
The page forces users to enter sensitive personal and financial details to download a public file
No official press statement exists on verified mainstream Kenyan broadcast channels
The article uses standard, professional typography and layout formats
